key_insight: In multimodal dementia prognosis—not cancer drug discovery—missing inputs can produce phantom attributions and misleading AI-generated explanations, while checks against restored data improve faithfulness.
clinical_relevance: The findings highlight a reliability concern for clinician-facing prognostic reports when tests such as amyloid PET or cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers are unavailable.
method: Masked every subset of four costly modalities in 307 ADNI participants to predict 36-month progression from mild cognitive impairment to Alzheimer’s disease.
Restored masked data to measure how missing evidence actually changed predictions.
Compared five missing-data strategies and evaluated 51,200 reports from four language models under four prompting regimes.
evidence_signal: All five strategies attributed 12%–23% of predictions to unobserved modalities; checking claims against executed restorations raised accuracy about missing-test effects from 27%–41% to 69% for open-weight narrators and 99.9% for a proprietary model.
watch_item: Evaluation used artificially masked complete cases, so performance under real-world missingness and in other patient populations remains uncertain.
paper_title: Faithful Explanations under Missing Modalities in Multimodal Dementia Prognosis
